newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Housewares warns on 1997/98 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Housewares warns on 1997/98 earnings.

text.p: South African household goods and mail order firm Housewares Ltd said on Thursday the group was unlikely to show improved earnings in the new financial year.

"There is little indication that the retail credit environment will improve in the short term and we expect difficult trading conditions to persist particularly over the next six months," Housewares said in a statement accompanying its year results.
The firm, which in March warned on a fall in year profits, earlier reported a 38.5 percent fall in headline earnings per share to 17.4 cents in the year to March 31 from 28.3 a year ago.

Housewares, which blamed a harsh credit environment for the fall in earnings especially in the direct sales business, said it considered it prudent not to declare a dividend. It said the mail order unit Glomail had done well.
It also planned to "right size" the sales division and reduce overhead costs. At the same time its information technology would be enhanced.

"Whilst we anticipate continued growth from Glomail, it is unlikely that the group as a whole will show improved earnings during the next financial year, as the actions being implemented will not necessarily yield immediate benefits," it said.
Housewares announced the appointment of joint managing director Steve Hochstadter as group chief executive, taking over from Mervyn Gutkin who will retain his role as executive chairman.
